mainTopic: Which פסוקים of the יום הכיפורים service are out of order, followed by אגדה about 'life' and about תלמידי חכמים.
overview: The ברייתא says the whole יום הכיפורים section in ויקרא is in order except the פסוק ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד. רב חסדא proves this from a tradition of five טבילות and ten קידושין: read in order, the פסוקים give only three. רבי זירא suggests the extra changes could come from the שעיר הנעשה בחוץ instead, but אביי shows from ויצא ועשה that the rams come right after the inner service. רבא adds a proof from the extra words אשר לבש, and when רבה בר רב שילא challenges it, ויצא ועשה again answers. The גמרא then notes that the פסוקים about burning the fats and burning the פר and שעיר are also out of order, so the exception means 'this פסוק and onward.' אביי and רבא show from המשלח and יעמד חי that the פסוקים, not the משנה, are the ones out of order. The amud ends with אגדה: the משלח greeting the כהן גדול, teachings about 'life,' and three sayings of רבי ברכיה about תלמידי חכמים, the last of which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Every verse is in order except this one
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by stating that the whole יום הכיפורים section is written in order, except for the פסוק of ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the whole section is written in order, except for this verse.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of a ברייתא. It says that one פסוק, where the כהן גדול goes back in to remove the כף and מחתה, is the only one in the section that is out of order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the עבודה follows the order of the פסוקים in ויקרא ט״ז. This פסוק (ט״ז:כ״ג) is written before the פסוק about the rams (ט״ז:כ״ד), but it is actually done after the rams. That claim of being out of order is what the גמרא will now question.

keyTerms.meaning: Section of the Torah (here, ויקרא ט״ז)

steps.confusionAlert: Not the whole section is out of order. Only this one פסוק is moved later; everything else is done exactly as written.

phrases.english: As the entire section
phrases.notes: Continuation of a ברייתא that began on the previous amud

phrases.english: was stated in order,
except for this verse.
phrases.notes: ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד (ויקרא ט״ז:כ״ג)

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכׇּל הַפָּרָשָׁה כּוּלָּהּ נֶאֶמְרָה עַל הַסֵּדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from the previous section of the דף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the פסוקים of the יום הכיפורים service are in order except ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד, which is done later.

steps.title: How do we know this verse is out of order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source or reason behind the claim that this פסוק is out of order.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we should think this פסוק is out of order. This short question sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we assume the Torah's order is the order of the עבודה. Saying one פסוק is out of order is a big claim, so the גמרא wants proof.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the ברייתא's claim in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What proves that ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד is out of order?

steps.title: רב חסדא: the tradition of five immersions and ten sanctifications
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא cites a tradition that the כהן גדול does five טבילות and ten קידושין on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We have a tradition that the כהן גדול immerses five times and washes his hands and feet ten times on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a known tradition: on יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול immerses five times and washes his hands and feet ten times. He will use this number in the next step to prove the פסוק is out of order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every time the כהן גדול switches between the gold clothes and the white clothes, he washes his hands and feet, immerses, puts on the new clothes, and washes again. So each change means one טבילה and two קידושין. Five טבילות means five changes of clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: We have a tradition (we learned it as a received teaching)
Washing of the hands and feet (קידוש ידים ורגלים)

steps.confusionAlert: Here קידושין does not mean marriage. It means the כהן washing his hands and feet from the כיור.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: We have a tradition,
five immersions and ten sanctifications
the High Priest immerses and sanctifies
phrases.notes: Two קידושין for each טבילה: one before, one after

phrases.english: on that day,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tradition requires five טבילות and ten קידושין on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This number becomes the fixed point that every reading of the פסוקים must match.

steps.title: In order, the verses give only three immersions
steps.stepSummary: If every פסוק were in order, there would be only three טבילות and six קידושין. So this פסוק must happen later to reach five and ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the verses are written in their order, you find only three immersions and six sanctifications.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his proof. If we follow the פסוקים in order, we get only three changes of clothes, not five, so the tradition forces us to move this one פסוק later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read in order, the day goes gold (תמיד), white (the special עבודה), gold (rams and the rest), which is three טבילות. If removing the כף and מחתה happens after the rams, the כהן גדול must change back to white and then to gold again. That adds two טבילות and four קידושין, reaching five and ten.

keyTerms.meaning: They are written in their order
You will not find it (you cannot reach the number)

steps.whatToRemember: The tradition of five טבילות and ten קידושין proves that ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד (removing the כף and מחתה) comes after the rams, even though it is written before them.

phrases.english: And if you say they are written in their order,
you do not find it
except as three immersions and six sanctifications.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the tradition from step 3 to prove the ברייתא's claim in step 1
steps.raayaObject: The claim that ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד is out of order
steps.raayaSupportSource: The tradition of five טבילות and ten קידושין, compared with the count you get reading in order (three and six)

steps.title: רבי זירא: maybe the extra change comes from the outer goat
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects: perhaps the white-clothes עבודה is interrupted by the שעיר הנעשה בחוץ, done in gold clothes. That would add the missing changes without moving any פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged it: But perhaps he interrupts it with the goat that is done outside!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רב חסדא's proof. He suggests another way to get five טבילות that keeps all the פסוקים in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שעיר הנעשה בחוץ (the מוסף goat) is written in במדבר, not in ויקרא, so placing it in the middle does not break the order of ויקרא. If the כהן גדול changes to gold for that goat and then back to white, that adds two טבילות and four קידושין. So the count of five and ten no longer proves that our פסוק is out of order.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat offered outside (the מוסף goat, done in the courtyard in gold clothes)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the שעיר of the white-clothes עבודה whose blood goes inside. This is a different goat, the מוסף goat, offered outside in the gold clothes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to it:
But perhaps he interrupts it
with the goat that is performed outside!
phrases.notes: The מוסף goat from במדבר כ״ט, offered in the gold clothes

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's proof that the tradition of five טבילות forces ובא אהרן אל אהל מועד out of order
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another way to reach five טבילות and ten קידושין: insert the שעיר הנעשה בחוץ, which is not in ויקרא, into the middle of the white-clothes עבודה. Then all the פסוקים in ויקרא can stay in order, and the proof fails.

steps.title: אביי: right after leaving, he offers the rams
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רבי זירא from the פסוק ויצא ועשה את עולתו. It shows that right after the first exit, the כהן גדול offers the two rams. So there is no room to break up the white-clothes עבודה with the שעיר הנעשה בחוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says, 'And he shall go out and offer his burnt-offering.' This means that right after his first going-out, he offers his ram and the ram of the people.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא's challenge. He shows from a פסוק that the white-clothes עבודה cannot be interrupted the way רבי זירא suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ויצא teaches that as soon as the כהן גדול finishes the inner service and comes out, he goes straight to the two rams. So there is no gap for an extra gold-clothes interruption in the middle. The only way to reach five טבילות and ten קידושין is the later return to the קודש הקדשים, so ובא אהרן must be out of order.

keyTerms.meaning: His ram and the people's ram

phrases.english: Abaye said: the verse says:
"And he shall go out and offer his burnt-offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:כד

phrases.english: right from the first going-out he performs
his ram and the ram of the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual proof that blocks the suggested interruption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The white-clothes עבודה could be broken up by the שעיר הנעשה בחוץ, which would supply the missing changes
steps.terutzMaskana: ויצא means the rams come right after the inner service, so the extra changes must come from the later re-entry

steps.title: רבא: 'which he wore' means clothes he already wore
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different proof. The extra words אשר לבש mean garments he had worn before, taken off, and put on again. That fits only a later point in the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says, 'And he shall take off the linen garments.' It did not need to add 'which he wore.' Does a person take off anything except what he is wearing?! So why does it say 'which he wore'? It means garments he had already worn before.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, separate proof that ובא אהרן is out of order. His proof comes from extra words in that very פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Obviously a person can only take off what he has on, so the words אשר לבש look extra. רבא reads them as 'which he had already worn earlier.' This means the כהן גדול had worn the white clothes, switched to gold, and then put white on again. That describes the later trip to remove the spoon and pan, so the פסוק belongs later.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק did not need to say this (the words look extra)
That he had already worn before

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse says:
"And he shall take off the linen garments"
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:כג

phrases.english: for the verse did not need to say "which he wore";

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם אָדָם פּוֹשֵׁט אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁלּוֹבֵשׁ?!
phrases.english: does a person take off anything but what he is wearing?!
Rather, why does the verse say "which he wore"?
It means what he had already worn before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent proof, alongside אביי's, that ובא אהרן is out of order. Step 8 shows that by itself it does not get past רבי זירא's goat-interruption idea.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading extra words in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ובא אהרן could be in its written place
steps.terutzMaskana: אשר לבש shows the white clothes were worn a second time, so the פסוק describes a later stage

steps.title: רבה בר רב שילא: maybe the outside goat explains 'already worn'
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא challenges רבא's proof. If the white service was broken up by the שעיר הנעשה בחוץ, he would also have 'already worn' the white clothes, even with the פסוק in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא challenged this: But say that he interrupts it with the goat that is offered outside!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא attacks רבא's proof by bringing back רבי זירא's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the כהן גדול did white, then switched to gold for the outside goat, then went back to white. Then by ובא אהרן he would also have 'already worn' the white clothes. So אשר לבש does not prove the פסוק is out of order.

keyTerms.meaning: That he interrupts (breaks up the service)
The goat offered outside (the מוסף goat, done in gold clothes)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila challenged it:
But say that he interrupts it
with the goat that is offered outside!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's proof in step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The interruption with the outside goat also creates a second wearing of the white clothes. So the words do not force the פסוק to be out of order.

steps.title: Answer: the verse 'he shall go out and offer' rules this out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with אביי's פסוק ויצא ועשה. The rams come right after the inner service, so there is no interruption with the outside goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And he shall go out and offer'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבה בר רב שילא by pointing back to the פסוק אביי used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויצא ועשה shows that the inner service leads straight into the rams, with no break. That removes the possible interruption. So אשר לבש can only mean the later re-entry, and רבא's proof stands.

phrases.english: But it is written: "And he shall go out and offer"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 using אביי's פסוק from step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a פסוק that blocks the alternative
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outside goat could interrupt the white service
steps.terutzMaskana: No interruption is possible, so ובא אהרן is out of order
steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא prove that ובא אהרן happens later in the day. ויצא ועשה blocks any break in the white-clothes service.

steps.title: Challenge: other verses also seem out of order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's claim that everything else is in order. The פסוק of burning the fats comes before the פסוק about burning the פר and שעיר. Yet the משנה shows the פר and שעיר are burned first, and the fats only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the whole section really said in order? But the פסוקים say: 'And the fat of the sin-offering he shall burn on the altar,' and after that: 'And the bull of the sin-offering and the goat of the sin-offering…' Yet we learned in the משנה: One who watches the כהן גדול reading does not see the bull and goat being burned. And the fats of the sin-offering are burned only after that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the starting claim of the ברייתא. It argues that even other פסוקים in the section are not in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוקים, burning the fats on the מזבח comes before taking the פר and שעיר outside to burn. But the משנה shows the פר and שעיר are burned while the כהן גדול reads the תורה, and the fats are burned only after the reading. So the actual order is the reverse of the written order.

keyTerms.meaning: In order (in the order they are done)
The bull and goat that are burned outside
The parts of the sin-offering burned on the מזבח
Yet we learned in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Two different burnings are involved. The אימורים (fats) are burned on the מזבח, while the whole פר and שעיר are burned outside the camp. Do not mix them up.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַפָּרָשָׁה כּוּלָּהּ נֶאֶמְרָה עַל הַסֵּדֶר?
phrases.english: And was the entire section said in order?
But the verses are written:
"And the fat of the sin-offering he shall burn on the altar"
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:כה

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר: ״וְאֵת פַּר הַחַטָּאת וְאֵת שְׂעִיר הַחַטָּאת״,
phrases.english: and afterward: "And the bull of the sin-offering and the goat of the sin-offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:כז

phrases.english: yet we learned in the Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹאֶה אֶת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל כְּשֶׁהוּא קוֹרֵא —
phrases.english: One who sees the High Priest while he is reading
does not see the bull and goat being burned.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ אֵמוּרֵי חַטָּאת בָּתַר הָכִי מַקְטֵיר לְהוּ!
phrases.english: Whereas the sacrificial parts of the sin-offering he burns only after that!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הַפָּרָשָׁה כּוּלָּהּ נֶאֶמְרָה עַל הַסֵּדֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's claim from step 1 and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the whole section is in order except ובא אהרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The written order (fats, then פר and שעיר) is the reverse of the real order from the משנה (פר and שעיר burned during the reading, fats after it). So there is a second out-of-order spot.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge holds, the ברייתא's statement that only one פסוק is out of order needs to be explained or limited.

steps.title: The exception covers this verse and onward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's exception is not only one פסוק. It covers 'this פסוק and onward.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that the ברייתא means: everything is in order except from this verse and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 10. It says the ברייתא's words 'except one פסוק' really mean the order stops being exact from that point onward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 the problem was that the fats פסוק comes before the burning of the פר and שעיר, but the משנה does them the other way around. The answer widens the exception to 'this פסוק and onward.' So the order of the פסוקים in that last section is not the order of the עבודה, and the clash with the משנה disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / read it this way (the גמרא suggests a new reading)

phrases.english: Say:
phrases.notes: The גמרא offers a new way to read the ברייתא.

phrases.english: except from this verse and onward.
phrases.notes: The exception is not just one פסוק. It is a whole section from that point on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10 by rereading the ברייתא's exception more broadly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא's wording: the exception applies to a whole section, not one פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא meant only one single פסוק was out of order, so the fats-before-burning order of the פסוקים seemed to clash with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: From the exception פסוק onward, the פסוקים are not in the order of the עבודה, so the משנה's order stands.

steps.title: Why move the verses instead of the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why decide that the פסוקים are out of order? Maybe the משנה is the one that has the order wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you rearrange the verses? Rearrange the משנה instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 11. It asks why we assume the פסוקים are out of place, when we could just as well say the משנה's order is the one to adjust.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 fixed the clash by saying the Torah's order is not the real order of the עבודה. The challenge asks for a reason to prefer that choice. Without a reason, we could keep the פסוקים in order, so the fats would come first, and change the משנה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why do you prefer this option?)
You rearrange / you treat it as out of order

phrases.english: And what did you see
phrases.notes: A standard formula: why did you pick this option over the other one?

phrases.english: that you rearrange the verses?
phrases.notes: You said the פסוקים are out of order.

phrases.english: Rearrange the Mishnah instead!
phrases.notes: Why not say the משנה's order is the one to change?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי חָזֵית דִּמְשַׁבְּשַׁתְּ קְרָאֵי, שַׁבֵּישׁ מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 11 by asking why it chose to change the פסוקים rather than the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 11 that the פסוקים from the exception onward are out of order.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are two sources that disagree, the פסוקים and the משנה. Choosing to change the פסוקים needs a reason. Otherwise the משנה could just as easily be the one to change.

steps.title: אביי: 'the one who sends' and 'the one who burns' are alike
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves the פסוקים are out of order. The Torah uses the same style for 'the one who sends' the שעיר and 'the one who burns.' The sending clearly happened earlier, so the burning also happened earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says 'And the one who sends…' and 'And the one who burns.' Just as the sending was done earlier, so too the burning was done earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from Step 12. He gives a reason from the פסוקים themselves to say they are not written in the order of the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the one who sends the שעיר to עזאזל comes after the fats פסוק, yet the sending clearly happened earlier in the day. The burner is written in the same way ('והשורף'), so אביי compares the two. Just like the sending, the burning of the פר and שעיר also happened earlier, before the fats. That matches the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the one who sends (the שעיר to עזאזל)
And the one who burns (the remains of the פר and שעיר)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is talking about the order of the words. He means the actions happened before the fats, even though the פסוקים about them are written after the fats פסוק.

phrases.english: Abaye said,
the verse states:
"And the one who sends … and the one who burns."
phrases.notes: Two פסוקים (ויקרא טז:כו and טז:כח) written in the same style.

phrases.english: Just as the one who sends is from earlier —
phrases.notes: The שעיר was already sent before the fats were burned.

phrases.english: so too the one who burns is from earlier.
phrases.notes: So the burning of the פר and שעיר also came before the fats, just like the משנה says.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אָמַר קְרָא: וְהַמְשַׁלֵּחַ וְהַשּׂוֹרֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by giving a reason from the פסוקים to treat them as out of order.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A proof from the פסוקים themselves: a comparison between two matching phrases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With no reason to prefer one side, the משנה could be the one out of order.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'sender' פסוק describes an earlier action, so the 'burner' פסוק does too. That shows the פסוקים are out of order, and the משנה is right.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method in the גמרא. When two sources clash, it looks for a hint inside the פסוקים to decide which one to read differently.

steps.title: On the contrary: compare the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on אביי. The comparison could go the other way: just as the burning is done 'now,' after the fats, the sending is also done 'now.'
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: just as the one who burns does so now, so too the one who sends does so now!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects אביי's proof from Step 13. It says the same comparison can be flipped around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי used the sender to teach about the burner. The גמרא says you could just as well use the burner, written after the fats, to teach about the sender. Then the sending would also come after the fats. Since the comparison works both ways, it does not prove which order is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary (the opposite argument is just as strong)
Now (at this later point, after the fats)

phrases.english: On the contrary:
phrases.notes: The same logic can be turned around.

phrases.english: just as the one who burns is from now —
phrases.notes: The burning is written after the fats, so maybe it really is done then.

phrases.english: so too the one who sends is from now!
phrases.notes: Then the sending would also come later. The comparison proves nothing on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה: מָה שׂוֹרֵף דְּהַשְׁתָּא — אַף מְשַׁלֵּחַ דְּהַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof in Step 13 by showing the comparison can be reversed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The direction of אביי's comparison between משלח and שורף.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison works in both directions. Nothing shows that the sender teaches about the burner rather than the burner teaching about the sender.

steps.title: The word 'the one who sends' points to the past
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the pushback against אביי. The form 'והמשלח' means 'the one who already sent,' so the sending happened earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the one who sends' means an action that was done earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי's proof against the pushback in step 14. It says the word 'והמשלח' itself shows the sending already happened before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 argued the comparison could run the other way, so the sending would also be happening 'now.' The גמרא answers that the comparison cannot run that way, because the word 'המשלח' by its own meaning describes someone who already sent the goat. So the past meaning of 'המשלח' decides the direction: the burning, described in the same style, also happened earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: And the one who sends (here read as: the one who already sent)

phrases.english: "And the one who sends"
phrases.notes: Quoting the word from the פסוק about the שעיר

phrases.english: implies that it was done earlier.
phrases.notes: The word itself describes a finished action

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the pushback of step 14 and restores אביי's proof
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linguistic reading: the word's own meaning fixes the time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison could go either way, so the sending might also be 'now,' after the fats.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'המשלח' means one who already sent, so the sending and the burning both happened earlier.

steps.title: רבא's proof: the goat only has to stay alive until the blood is given
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different proof from 'יעמד חי': the goat must stay alive only until the time of atonement, which is when the blood is sprinkled. After that it is sent away, so the sending happened early.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The פסוק says 'shall be stood alive.' Until when must it stay standing alive? Until the time of atonement. And when is the time of atonement? At the time the blood is put on, and no later.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second, separate proof that the sending of the שעיר happened early, before the fats were burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the goat must be 'stood alive' for atonement. רבא explains that this need lasts only until the atonement, which is the sprinkling of the blood inside. Once the blood is done, the goat is sent right away. That is before the fats are burned, so the פסוקים are not written in time order, and the משנה's order is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: The putting on (sprinkling) of the blood

steps.whatToRemember: The sending of the שעיר happens right after the blood is sprinkled, so the פסוקים about sending and burning are not in time order, and the משנה's order stands.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The verse states: "shall be stood alive"
phrases.notes: ויקרא ט״ז:י׳

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי יְהֵא זָקוּק לַעֲמוֹד חַי?
phrases.english: Until when must it stay standing alive?
Until the time of atonement.
And when is the time of atonement?
At the time the blood is put on, and no later.
phrases.notes: After that the goat is sent out immediately

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an independent proof for the same point אביי was making
steps.raayaObject: That the sending of the שעיר happened early, so the פסוקים are out of order and the משנה is correct
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'יעמד חי לכפר עליו', with the atonement identified as the sprinkling of the blood

steps.title: How the sender greets the כהן גדול after יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: When the משלח returns, if he meets the כהן גדול in the market he says, 'My master the כהן גדול, we did your mission.' If he meets him at home he says, 'The One Who gives life to the living, we did His mission.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who sent the goat comes back. If he finds the כהן גדול in the market, he says to him: 'My master, כהן גדול! We did your mission.' If he finds him in his house, he says to him: 'The One Who gives life to the living, we did His mission.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: what the man who led the שעיר away says when he meets the כהן גדול afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In public he gives the credit to the כהן גדול, to show him honor in front of people. In private he says the truth plainly: the mission really belonged to הקב״ה, called here 'מחיה חיים.' This phrase 'מחיה חיים' leads into the next two teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who sends the שעיר away
Mission; a task done on someone's behalf
The One Who gives life to the living (הקב״ה)

steps.confusionAlert: 'שליחותך' (your mission) and 'שליחותו' (His mission) differ by one letter. In public the mission is credited to the כהן גדול. At home it is credited to הקב״ה.

phrases.english: The one who sends comes back;
if he finds the High Priest in the market,
he says to him: My master, High Priest!
We have done your mission.
phrases.notes: Honor shown in public

phrases.english: If he finds him in his house,
he says to him: The One Who gives life to the living,
we have done His mission.
phrases.notes: In private the mission is credited to הקב״ה

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתֵי מְשַׁלֵּחַ, מְצָאוֹ בַּשּׁוּק לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the scene after the עבודה, no longer about the order of the עבודה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In public the sender credits the mission to the כהן גדול; in private he credits it to הקב״ה.

steps.title: The farewell blessing of the חכמים in פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports that when the חכמים of פומבדיתא parted from each other, they blessed each other: 'May the One Who gives life to the living give you long, good, and stable life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: When the Sages took leave of one another in פומבדיתא, they said this: 'May the One Who gives life to the living give you a long, good, and stable life.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the phrase 'מחיה חיים' just came up, the גמרא brings a related teaching from רבה: the parting blessing used by the חכמים of פומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side teaching connected only by the shared phrase 'מחיה חיים.' It shows that the חכמים used this name of הקב״ה when they blessed each other with a good life.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Torah center in בבל

phrases.english: Rabba said:
When the Sages take leave of one another
in Pumbedita, they say this:
"May the One Who gives life to the living give you
a long, good, and stable life."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: כִּי מִיפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מֵהֲדָדֵי בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected to step 17 by the shared phrase 'מחיה חיים'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים of פומבדיתא parted with the blessing 'מחיה חיים יתן לך חיים ארוכים וטובים ומתוקנין.'

steps.title: 'The lands of the living' means a place of markets
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'אתהלך לפני ה׳ בארצות החיים', רב יהודה explains that 'lands of the living' means a place with markets, where a person can easily get what he needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I shall walk before ה׳ in the lands of the living.' רב יהודה said: This is a place of markets.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the theme of 'חיים,' the גמרא brings רב יהודה's explanation of a פסוק in תהלים that speaks of 'the lands of the living.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה reads 'ארצות החיים' as a place where life is easy because food and needs can be bought in the market. דוד המלך, who moved from place to place, asked to always be in such a place.

phrases.english: "I shall walk before the Lord
in the lands of the living"
phrases.notes: תהלים קט״ז:ט׳

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
This is a place of markets.
phrases.notes: Where food and needs are easy to find

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶתְהַלֵּךְ לִפְנֵי ה׳ בְּאַרְצוֹת הַחַיִּים, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the side teachings linked by the word 'חיים'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ארצות החיים' means a place of markets, where a person's needs are easy to get.

steps.title: What are 'years of life'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק promising 'years of life.' It asks how some years can be 'of life' and others not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'For length of days, and years of life, and peace, will they add to you.' Are there years of life and years that are not of life?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from משלי and asks a question about one phrase in it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every year a person lives is a year of being alive. So the phrase 'years of life' sounds extra. The גמרא wants to know what special kind of year the פסוק is promising.

keyTerms.meaning: length of days, a long life
'and is it so that…?', a word that opens a puzzled question

phrases.english: "For length of days, and years of life,
phrases.notes: משלי ג:ב

phrases.english: and peace, will they add to you"
Are there, then, years of life
and years that are not of life?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the run of teachings about 'life' (מחיה חיים, ארצות החיים) with another פסוק that mentions life.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the seemingly extra phrase 'years of life' add?

steps.title: Years that turn from bad to good
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that 'years of life' are years in a person's life that turn from bad to good.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: These are the years of a person that turn over for him from bad to good.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question. 'Years of life' means good years, especially years that started out bad and became good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'life' means a life that is really worth living, not just being alive. So the פסוק is a promise that a person's hard times will turn into good times.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
These are the years of a person
that are turned over for him from bad to good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Years of life' are good years, the ones that change from bad to good.

steps.title: תלמידי חכמים are like women but strong like men
steps.stepSummary: רבי ברכיה reads the word 'אישים' in a פסוק as a hint to תלמידי חכמים. They look weak like women but do mighty work like men.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To you, men (אישים), I call.' רבי ברכיה said: These are תלמידי חכמים, who are like women but do mighty deeds like men.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי ברכיה explains why the פסוק uses the unusual word 'אישים' for men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual word for men is 'אנשים.' 'אישים' sounds like 'אשה' (woman), so רבי ברכיה sees both sides in it. תלמידי חכמים seem physically weak and stay out of worldly activity, like women of that time, yet in Torah learning they show real strength, like men.

keyTerms.meaning: men, an unusual form that sounds like 'אִשָּׁה' (woman)

phrases.english: "To you, men, do I call,"
phrases.notes: משלי ח:ד

phrases.english: Rabbi Berekhya said:
These are Torah scholars,
who are similar to women
but act with might like men.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲלֵיכֶם אִישִׁים אֶקְרָא, אָמַר רַבִּי בֶּרֶכְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה teaching. This one opens a series of statements by רבי ברכיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'אישים' hints to תלמידי חכמים, who seem weak like women but are mighty like men in Torah.

steps.title: Giving wine to תלמידי חכמים is like pouring wine on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי ברכיה teaches that a person who wants to pour wine on the מזבח should give wine to תלמידי חכמים. He uses the same פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ברכיה said: Whoever wants to pour wine on the מזבח should fill the throats of תלמידי חכמים with wine, as it says: 'To you, men (אישים), I call.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second teaching from רבי ברכיה on the same פסוק. Without a מזבח, giving wine to תלמידי חכמים takes the place of pouring wine on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'אישים' is read as sounding like 'אִשֶּׁה,' the word for the fire offerings on the מזבח. So תלמידי חכמים are compared to the מזבח itself, and supporting them is like bringing a נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: a fire offering on the מזבח, which sounds like 'אִישִׁים'

steps.confusionAlert: This uses the same פסוק as step 22, but reads 'אישים' differently. In step 22 it sounds like 'אִשָּׁה' (woman). Here it sounds like 'אִשֶּׁה' (fire offering on the מזבח).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Berekhya said:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹצֶה לְנַסֵּךְ יַיִן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ —
phrases.english: One who wishes to pour wine on the altar

phrases.aramaic: יְמַלֵּא גְּרוֹנָם שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים יַיִן,
phrases.english: should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine,
as it is stated: "To you, men, do I call."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement of רבי ברכיה, drawn from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving wine to תלמידי חכמים counts like pouring a wine offering on the מזבח.

steps.title: Marry a תלמיד חכם's daughter so Torah continues in the family
steps.stepSummary: רבי ברכיה advises that if Torah is stopping in a man's family, he should marry the daughter of a תלמיד חכם. He starts to bring a proof פסוק from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ברכיה said: If a person sees that Torah is stopping in his children, he should marry the daughter of a תלמיד חכם, as it says: 'Though its root grows old in the earth, and its trunk dies in the dust…'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third statement of רבי ברכיה. It gives practical advice for bringing Torah back into a family. The proof פסוק continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a tree whose root and trunk seem dead. The next words of the פסוק (איוב יד:ט), which appear on the next amud, say it will sprout again from the smell of water. Marrying into a Torah home is that 'water,' which brings Torah back to the next generation.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a family's Torah future can be renewed through whom one marries, even when it seems to be ending.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Berekhya said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם רוֹאֶה אָדָם שֶׁתּוֹרָה פּוֹסֶקֶת מִזַּרְעוֹ —
phrases.english: If a person sees that Torah is ceasing from his offspring,
he should marry the daughter of a Torah scholar,
as it is stated: "Though its root grows old in the earth,
phrases.notes: איוב יד:ח

phrases.english: and its trunk dies in the dust
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי בֶּרֶכְיָה: אִם רוֹאֶה אָדָם שֶׁתּוֹרָה פּוֹסֶקֶת מִזַּרְעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third statement in the chain of רבי ברכיה teachings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If Torah is fading from one's children, one should marry the daughter of a תלמיד חכם.
